proposals.expected_failure_mode: May shift peaks too early relative to observed hospitalizations, leading to systematic lead bias if true lag is closer to 3 weeks.
proposals.rationale: Primary local-search candidate around the current best; keeps SEIRS (waning/reinfection) while testing a slightly shorter reporting/admission lag to reduce sensitivity to a single timing alignment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can overfit to a particular validation-window timing; rolling splits may show instability if the effective lag varies across the season.
proposals.rationale: Anchor specification matching the previous best; serves as a stable baseline for comparing nearby delay adjustments without changing compartment complexity.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If hospitalization reporting is meaningfully delayed, forecasts will be phase-advanced and may miss the observed peak timing.
proposals.rationale: Adds a nearer-lag alternative to test robustness when admissions track incidence more tightly (e.g., faster care-seeking/reporting), potentially reducing delay-fragility by not relying on a longer fixed lag.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Likely timing misalignment (predicted peaks too early) if admissions lag incidence; may degrade fit around turning points.
proposals.rationale: No-delay mapping as a stress test for whether the lag is being used to compensate for model-shape mismatch; if competitive, it suggests dynamics (not delay) drive alignment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May under-capture multi-wave or prolonged tail behavior over the training horizon, yielding biased late-season levels.
proposals.rationale: Secondary check on whether the SIRS loop is truly required versus delay-driven alignment; keeps observation structure identical to the best while simplifying dynamics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Weak identifiability in short series can cause unstable decomposition between I and H, leading to over-parameterized dynamics and poorer generalization.
proposals.rationale: Minority inclusion to test whether an explicit hospitalization pathway improves timing alignment without relying on a fixed delay; I+H can soften identifiability issues versus H-only by allowing the observed rate to reflect combined infectious burden and admissions.
